name: AI Image Disclosure Helper
description: Generate the correct AI-generated / AI-assisted disclosure note for Adobe Stock, Shutterstock or Freepik so you never miss the checkbox or caption requirement.
body:
Platform policies change — verify the current rules on the platform before submitting.

Disclosure note

Select options and click generate to see the required disclosure text.

Checklist
howto: Choose the platform you are submitting to.
Select how the image was created — fully AI-generated, AI-assisted, or no AI.
Optionally add your own notes describing the AI tools used.
Click Generate disclosure note to get the exact phrasing for that platform.
Copy the note into the disclosure field of your submission and tick the disclosure checkbox if required.
features: Platform-specific disclosure phrasing for Adobe Stock, Shutterstock and Freepik
Separate handling for fully generated vs AI-assisted images
Custom notes appended to the disclosure
A checklist of the disclosure requirements each platform expects

faq.q: Does every platform require AI disclosure?
faq.a: Yes, all major stock platforms require you to disclose AI-generated or AI-assisted content. Failing to do so can lead to rejection or account suspension, so it is safer to always disclose when AI was used in any significant way.

faq.q: What is the difference between AI-generated and AI-assisted?
faq.a: Fully AI-generated means the core image was produced by an AI generator. AI-assisted means a real photograph or artwork was edited or enhanced with AI tools. The platforms treat these slightly differently, and this tool reflects those differences.

faq.q: Is this note what the platform will show buyers?
faq.a: No. The note is the disclosure text you attach to your submission metadata. It informs reviewers and buyers that AI was used — it is not the same as the caption buyers see.

faq.q: Can I rely on this tool for legal advice?
faq.a: No. It is a practical helper based on common platform rules. Platform policies change frequently — always double-check the current rules before submitting.
